title: Positive cohomology vanishes for nonnegative projective twists over a ring
statement: For a commutative ring A (including the zero ring), N a natural number, m a nonnegative integer and q a positive natural number, H^q(P^N_A,O(m)) is zero. O(m) is the projective twist [def-pc-projective-space-twist] and H is module right-derived global sections [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. No Noetherian hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 01XT, Lemma on cohomology of projective-space twists, nonnegative-twist case; monomial contraction used in Tag 01YS (4)

proof.text: Build explicitly the linear isomorphism between the standard-cover twist Cech complex, with scalars restricted along the structure morphism A → Gamma(P,O), and the Laurent-monomial complex. On an intersection indexed by sigma, send finite Laurent coefficient families to their monomial sections; the existing monomial section basis proves bijectivity, and the restriction formula proves compatibility with differentials. The affine-cover Leray comparison identifies ordinary twist cohomology with this complex homology. In degree p+1>0, use the monomial contracting homotopy. For an exponent vector with a nonnegative coordinate, the homotopy identity shows every cocycle is a boundary. If every coordinate is negative then the sum is negative (there are N+1 coordinates), so it is not m; all such coefficients are zero. Thus the complex is exact in every positive degree, including degrees above N and the case N=0. Transport IsZero through the explicit comparisons and the module-cohomology source comparison.
